X had signed composer S.D. Burman for the music of Y, a movie that turned out to be a landmark in his career. SD had prepared two tunes for a particular song, Z, in the film. After X picked one and left the studio, SD's son, Pancham, caught up with him on the stairs and said he preferred the other tune, and gave his reasons. The director was convinced, but Pancham refused to go back upstairs and break the news to his father: "Then come up and tell my father that because I'm not going to." Despite their trepidation, SD didn’t fuss over the change since both were his compositions,
Z was not planned as a single take. After the recording, X kept listening to it, trying to figure out the picturisation. He realized there was simply no place to cut - doing so would kill the impact. He borrowed a round trolley from Guru Dutt's production company, one of only two such trolleys in the industry at the time, and filmed it in one continuous shot. Years later, Mani Ratnam visited X’s family and admitted he had tried to replicate the single-take technique twice but could never match the impact.
